steps.message: Let's update `app/models/notification/pushing.rb` to use `after_save_commit` and re-run our tests!
steps.reasoning_content:
**The After-Commit Callback Conundrum**

Alright, let's break this down. That `_commit_callbacks` output – `[[:after, #<Proc:... line 27>], [:after, #<Proc:... line 26>], [:after, #<Proc:... line 25>], [:after, :push_later]]` – immediately caught my eye. Only one `:push_later`? That's not right. I knew something was amiss with how Rails' `after_commit` callbacks work.

Here's the problem: I had two `after_commit` calls using the *same* method symbol, `:push_later`, but with different conditions: `after_create_commit :push_later` and `after_update_commit :push_later, if: :source_id_previously_changed?`. Active Support's callback system *deduplicates* callbacks with the same name. So, the second definition overwrites the first. The one targeting updates, took the place of the one intended for new records. *Classic Rails gotcha!*

Looking at the Rails internals, specifically `ActiveRecord::Transactions::ClassMethods`, `after_create_commit :foo` calls `set_callback(:commit, :after, :foo, on: :create)`. `after_update_commit :foo, if: ...` calls `set_callback(:commit, :after, :foo, on: :update, if: ...)`.  In ActiveSupport, re-registering the same callback name on the same chain (`:commit` in this case) *removes* the previous one. Unless... you handle it correctly.

The key is to combine the callbacks correctly. Either I can write one `after_commit` call, like: `after_commit :push_later, on: %i[ create update ], if: :should_push?` or an `after_create_commit -> { push_later }` or `after_commit :push_later, on: :create` with `after_save_commit :push_later, if: :source_id_previously_changed?`.

But wait, `source_id_previously_changed?` is actually `true` on *create* as well, because the `source_id` is changing from `nil` to a UUID! That explains why pushing isn't occurring on create, only on update!

So the best solution here, I think, is: `after_save_commit :push_later, if: -> { previously_new_record? || source_id_previously_changed? }`. This registers *one* callback that handles both create and update scenarios. On create, `previously_new_record?` will be `true`, and on update when the `source_id` changes,  `source_id_previously_changed?` will be `true`.  Perfect!  And, importantly, it won't run on destroy because we're only targeting `:create` and `:update`.

Thank goodness for that test and inspecting `_commit_callbacks`! Caught a subtle bug.

Oh, and in our Mocha test, the `WebPush.payload_send(message: ..., endpoint: ...)` call is using keyword arguments (Ruby 3+), so `.with { |**args| ... }` cleanly receives those keyword arguments. That test setup is good.

Time to fix `app/models/notification/pushing.rb`, adjust the `**args` in the test, and re-run those tests. Let's get this done.

module Notification::Pushing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_save_commit :push_later, if: :should_push?
  end

  def push_later
    Notification::PushJob.perform_later(self) if pushable?
  end

  def push_now
    return unless pushable? && source.present? && card.present?

    path = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.card_path(card, script_name: account.slug)

    user.push_subscriptions.find_each do |subscription|
      subscription.push(title: title, body: body, path: path)
    rescue WebPush::Error, Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, SocketError, SystemCallError => error
      Rails.error.report(error, context: { notification_id: id, push_subscription_id: subscription.id })
    end
  end

  private
    def should_push?
      previously_new_record? || source_id_previously_changed?
    end

    def pushable?
      Push.configured? && user.active? && account.active? && user.push_subscriptions.any?
    end
end
EOF

    assert_equal card_path(event.card, script_name: @kevin.account.slug), captured_payload.dig("options", "data", "path")
  end

  test "pushes mention notification with tray mention title, body, and card path" do
    david_sub = @david.push_subscriptions.create!(
      endpoint: "https://web.push.apple.com/david-iphone",
      p256dh_key: @p256dh,
      auth_key: @auth
    )
    notifications(:logo_mentioned_david).destroy
    mention = mentions(:logo_comment_david_mention_by_jz)
    expected_path = card_path(mention.card, script_name: @david.account.slug)

    captured_payload = nil
    WebPush.expects(:payload_send).with do |**args|
      captured_payload = JSON.parse(args[:message])
      args[:endpoint] == david_sub.endpoint
    end.once

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Notification::PushJob do
      Notification.create!(user: @david, source: mention, creator: mention.mentioner)
    end

    assert_equal "#{mention.mentioner.first_name} @mentioned you", captured_payload["title"]
    assert_equal mention.source.mentionable_content.truncate(200), captured_payload.dig("options", "body")
    assert_equal expected_path, captured_payload.dig("options", "data", "path")
  end

  test "pushes when an existing notification for the same card is updated with a new source" do
    existing = notifications(:layout_commented_kevin)
    card = existing.card

    captured_payload = nil
    WebPush.expects(:payload_send).with do |**args|
      captured_payload = JSON.parse(args[:message])
      true
    end.once

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: [ NotifyRecipientsJob, Notification::PushJob ] do
      card.comments.create!(body: "Follow-up on layout", creator: @david)
    end

    assert_equal "RE: #{card.title}", captured_payload["title"]
    assert_equal "Follow-up on layout", captured_payload.dig("options", "body")
    assert_equal card_path(card, script_name: @kevin.account.slug), captured_payload.dig("options", "data", "path")
  end

  test "reading and unreading a notification does not send a push" do
    notification = notifications(:layout_commented_kevin)

    WebPush.expects(:payload_send).never

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Notification::PushJob do
      notification.read
      notification.unread
    end
  end

  test "does not push for cancelled accounts" do
    @kevin.account.cancel(initiated_by: @david)
    notifications(:layout_commented_kevin).destroy

    WebPush.expects(:payload_send).never

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Notification::PushJob do
      Notification.create!(user: @kevin, source: events(:layout_commented), creator: @david)
    end
  end

  test "continues delivering to remaining devices when one push service fails" do
    second_sub = @kevin.push_subscriptions.create!(
      endpoint: "https://updates.push.services.mozilla.com/wpush/v2/kevin-phone",
      p256dh_key: @p256dh,
      auth_key: @auth

    stub_request(:post, @subscription.endpoint).to_return(status: 500, body: "Internal Error")
    second_stub = stub_request(:post, second_sub.endpoint).to_return(status: 201)

    notifications(:layout_commented_kevin).destroy

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Notification::PushJob do
      Notification.create!(user: @kevin, source: events(:layout_commented), creator: @david)
    end

    assert_requested second_stub
  end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class PushNotificationsTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @user = users(:david)
    sign_in_as @user
  end

  test "shows help copy when browser blocks notifications" do
    visit notifications_settings_url

    assert_text "Push notifications are off for this device"

    page.execute_script <<~JS
      Object.defineProperty(Notification, "permission", { get: () => "default", configurable: true })
      Notification.requestPermission = async () => {
        Object.defineProperty(Notification, "permission", { get: () => "denied", configurable: true })
        return "denied"
      }
    JS

    find("[data-controller='notifications'] .switch").click

    assert_text "Turn on notifications for this website."
    assert find("[data-notifications-target='toggle']", visible: :all).disabled?
  end

  test "subscribes and unsubscribes current device from notification settings" do
    visit notifications_settings_url

    assert_text "Push notifications are off for this device"

    page.execute_script <<~JS
      let activeSubscription = null
      const mockSubscription = {
        endpoint: "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/system-test-device",
        toJSON: () => ({
          endpoint: "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/system-test-device",
          keys: {
            p256dh: "BNcRdreALRFXTkOOUHK1EtK2wtaz5Ry4YfYCA_0QTpQtUbVlUls0VJXg7A8u-Ts1XbjhazAkj7I99e8QcYP7DkM",
            auth: "tBHItJI5svbpez7KI4CCXg"
          }
        }),
        unsubscribe: async () => {
          activeSubscription = null
          return true
        }
      }

      const mockRegistration = {
        pushManager: {
          getSubscription: async () => activeSubscription,
          subscribe: async ({ userVisibleOnly, applicationServerKey }) => {
            window.__subscribedServerKeyLength = applicationServerKey.byteLength
            window.__subscribedUserVisibleOnly = userVisibleOnly
            activeSubscription = mockSubscription
            return mockSubscription
          }
        }
      }

      Object.defineProperty(Notification, "permission", { get: () => "default", configurable: true })
      Notification.requestPermission = async () => {
        Object.defineProperty(Notification, "permission", { get: () => "granted", configurable: true })
        return "granted"
      }

      navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration = async () => mockRegistration
      Object.defineProperty(navigator.serviceWorker, "ready", {
        get: () => Promise.resolve(mockRegistration),
        configurable: true
      })
    JS

    find("[data-controller='notifications'] .switch").click

    assert_selector "[data-controller='notifications'].notifications--on"
    assert_text "Push notifications are on for this device"

    assert_equal 65, page.evaluate_script("window.__subscribedServerKeyLength")
    assert_equal true, page.evaluate_script("window.__subscribedUserVisibleOnly")

    subscription = @user.push_subscriptions.find_by(endpoint: "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/system-test-device")
    assert_not_nil subscription
    assert_equal "BNcRdreALRFXTkOOUHK1EtK2wtaz5Ry4YfYCA_0QTpQtUbVlUls0VJXg7A8u-Ts1XbjhazAkj7I99e8QcYP7DkM", subscription.p256dh_key
    assert_equal "tBHItJI5svbpez7KI4CCXg", subscription.auth_key

    find("[data-controller='notifications'] .switch").click

    assert_no_selector "[data-controller='notifications'].notifications--on"
    assert_text "Push notifications are off for this device"
    assert_nil @user.push_subscriptions.find_by(endpoint: "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/system-test-device")
  end
end

module Push
  class << self
    def vapid_public_key
      ENV.fetch("VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY") do
        Rails.configuration.x.vapid.public_key || local_vapid_key&.public_key
      end&.strip

    def vapid_private_key

        Rails.configuration.x.vapid.private_key || local_vapid_key&.private_key
      end&.strip
    end

    def configured?
      vapid_public_key.present? && vapid_private_key.present?
    end

    def vapid_identification
      {
        subject: vapid_subject,
        public_key: vapid_public_key,
        private_key: vapid_private_key
      }
    end

    private
      def local_vapid_key
        if Rails.env.test?
          @test_vapid_key ||= WebPush.generate_key
        elsif Rails.env.development?
          @development_vapid_key ||= load_or_generate_development_vapid_key
        end
      end

      def load_or_generate_development_vapid_key
        path = Rails.root.join("tmp/vapid.json")
        if path.exist?

          WebPush::VapidKey.from_keys(keys[:public_key], keys[:private_key])
        else

            path.dirname.mkpath

      end

        ENV.fetch("VAPID_SUBJECT") do
          "mailto:#{Mail::Address.new(ApplicationMailer.default[:from]).address}"
        end
      end
  end
end

class Users::PushSubscriptionsController < ApplicationController
  wrap_parameters :push_subscription, include: %i[ endpoint p256dh_key auth_key ]

  before_action :set_user
  before_action :ensure_current_user

  def index
    render json: @user.push_subscriptions.select(:id, :endpoint, :created_at)
  end

  def create
    if subscription = @user.push_subscriptions.find_by(endpoint: push_subscription_params[:endpoint])
      subscription.update!(push_subscription_params.merge(user_agent: request.user_agent, session: Current.session))
      head :ok
    else
      @user.push_subscriptions.create!(push_subscription_params.merge(user_agent: request.user_agent, session: Current.session))
      head :created
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    retry
  end

  def destroy
    if params[:id].present?
      @user.push_subscriptions.find(params[:id]).destroy!
      head :no_content
    elsif endpoint = endpoint_param
      @user.push_subscriptions.destroy_by(endpoint: endpoint)
      head :no_content
    else
      head :bad_request
    end
  end

  private
    def set_user
      @user = Current.account.users.active.find(params[:user_id])
    end

    def ensure_current_user
      head :forbidden unless @user == Current.user
    end

    def push_subscription_params
      params.expect(push_subscription: [ :endpoint, :p256dh_key, :auth_key ])
    end

    def endpoint_param
      params[:endpoint].presence || params.dig(:push_subscription, :endpoint).presence
    end
end

class PushNotificationsTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @user = users(:david)
    sign_in_as @user
  end

  test "service worker registers and activates cleanly" do

      navigator.serviceWorker.ready.then((registration) => {

      }).catch((err) => done(err.message))

  end

        return "denied"
      }
    JS

    find("[data-controller='notifications'] .switch").click

    assert_text "Turn on notifications for this website."
    assert find("[data-notifications-target='toggle']", visible: :all).disabled?

steps.message:
Web push notifications have been implemented across the application:

### Summary of Changes
1. **VAPID Configuration (`Push`, `config/initializers/vapid.rb`, `app/views/layouts/shared/_head.html.erb`)**:
   - Reads `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` and `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` from environment variables (with credentials fallback and ephemeral local keys for development/test).
   - Exposes `<meta name="vapid-public-key">` to authenticated web clients when VAPID keys are configured.

2. **Push Subscriptions (`db/migrate/20261121210300_create_push_subscriptions.rb`, `PushSubscription`, `Users::PushSubscriptionsController`, `config/routes.rb`)**:
   - Added tenant-scoped `push_subscriptions` table (`endpoint`, `p256dh_key`, `auth_key`, `user_agent`, `user_id`, `session_id`, `account_id`).
   - Added `/users/:user_id/push_subscriptions` endpoints (`create`, `destroy`, `index`) accepting `push_subscription[endpoint, p256dh_key, auth_key]`, scoped strictly to `Current.user`.
   - Automatically cleans up subscriptions on expired/invalid/unauthorized push responses (`410`/`404`/`401`), session sign-out, and user deactivation.

3. **Tray-to-Push Delivery (`Notification::Pushing`, `Notification::PushJob`, `Event`, `Mention`, `app/views/pwa/service_worker.js.erb`)**:
   - Enqueues `Notification::PushJob` whenever a notification is created or updated with a new source in a user's tray.
   - Delivers Web Push payloads matching the tray's `title` and `body` along with the account-scoped card path (`options.data.path`).
   - Added `push` and `notificationclick` listeners to `/service-worker.js` to display the notification and focus or open the card URL.

4. **Notification Settings UI & Stimulus Controller (`app/views/notifications/settings/_push.html.erb`, `app/views/notifications/settings/show.html.erb`, `app/javascript/controllers/notifications_controller.js`)**:
   - Added the per-device Push Notifications toggle section to Notification Settings using `notifications.css` styles and the `_browser`, `_install`, and `_system` help copy partials when notifications are blocked or require web app installation.

5. **Tests**:
   - Added model, controller, PWA service worker, and headless Chrome system tests verifying subscription management, cryptographic VAPID signing & `aes128gcm` payload encryption, tray parity, and blocked-notification help copy.
